questionText: In biodiversity conservation assessment #116: Tropical Amazonian rainforest in South America harbours the greatest biodiversity on Earth. Why do the tropics support vastly greater biological diversity than temperate regions?

options.text: Tropical environments experience frequent glaciations promoting rapid speciation
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Tropical environments experience frequent glaciations promoting rapid speciation'.

options.text: Tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years, are less seasonal, more predictable, and receive higher solar energy
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: Tropical soils contain higher calcium carbonate concentrations
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Tropical soils contain higher calcium carbonate concentrations'.

options.text: Predators are completely absent from tropical ecosystems
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Predators are completely absent from tropical ecosystems'.

detailedSolution:
1. Ecologists propose three major hypotheses for high tropical diversity: (a) Speciation is a function of time; tropics remained undisturbed unlike glaciated temperate regions; (b) Tropical environments are less seasonal, more constant and predictable; (c) More solar energy is available in the tropics, contributing to higher productivity.
Hence Option B is correct.

questionText: Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod, and Maclyn McCarty purified biochemicals (proteins, DNA, RNA) from heat-killed S cells. Transformation of live R cells into S cells was inhibited ONLY when the extract was treated with which enzyme?

Hence Option B is correct.

questionText: In molecular diagnostic testing #115: When using a radioactive single-stranded probe to detect a mutated gene in cloned host cells via autoradiography, why does the mutated gene NOT appear on the photographic film?

topic: Cloning Vector Features and Selectable Markers
questionText:

Cloning vectors are engineered to facilitate the linking of foreign DNA and the selection of transformants. The plasmid pBR322 was one of the earliest artificial cloning vectors constructed. It contains an origin of replication (ori), which controls the copy number of linked DNA. It also contains two antibiotic resistance genes: ampicillin resistance (ampR) and tetracycline resistance (tetR), which act as selectable markers. questionText: Double fertilization in angiosperms involves two distinct fusion events known as:

questionText: In molecular cloning evaluation #53: Why do restriction endonucleases make staggered cuts leaving single-stranded overhanging stretches called 'sticky ends' on DNA?

options.text: Sticky ends prevent any circularization of plasmid vectors
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Sticky ends prevent any circularization of plasmid vectors'.

options.text: Sticky ends allow DNA polymerase to transcribe without RNA primers
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Sticky ends allow DNA polymerase to transcribe without RNA primers'.

options.text: Sticky ends are resistant to degradation by cellular exonucleases
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Sticky ends are resistant to degradation by cellular exonucleases'.

options.text: The sticky ends form hydrogen bonds readily with complementary sticky ends cut by the same enzyme, facilitating DNA ligase action
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

detailedSolution:
1. Restriction enzymes cut the strand of DNA a little away from the centre of the palindrome sites, between the same two bases on opposite strands, leaving single stranded overhangs called sticky ends.
2. These form hydrogen bonds with their complementary cut counterparts, which greatly facilitates the action of the enzyme DNA ligase.
Hence Option D is correct.

questionText: Which of the following was NOT a major reason why Mendel's pioneering work remained unrecognized until 1900?
